races.name: Betfred 'turbo Boost' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Em Four
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with Saffie Osborne claiming; sole win came over 6f on Good ground and similar-going record is thin (1 win from 15), so the soft test here is not a given despite the OK tag — needs a strong pace and a clear lane late.

runners_data.name: Logi Bear
runners_data.note: David Probert partners this three-year-old hold-up type who won over 6f on Standard and placed on Good; the soft ground is untested but form over this trip is solid, and a 16-day turnaround for the John Butler yard (1 winner from 16 in 14 days) is a mild negative on trainer strike-rate.

runners_data.name: Twirler
runners_data.note: Michael Attwater five-year-old with a genuine hold-up profile — though shown in midfield here, it is a true closer operating out of its natural position given the density of rear-runners in this field; has placed on soft ground over 6f and carries live each-way claims if the pace truly injures those up front, though the style displacement is a real handicap.

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon handler sends out this four-year-old who is a natural hold-up type shuffled into a midfield slot on the map; all five recent runs are on Good or Good to Soft at best, and the step into soft proper is an untested variable — the trainer's 14-day record (0 from 37) is a significant dampener.

runners_data.name: Proof
runners_data.note: Charles Hills three-year-old returning after 69 days off; won over 5f on Standard but is another genuine closer placed into midfield because the back of the field is already full, and that style displacement — combined with a 69-day absence — makes its chance harder to assess despite one win from four runs on soft-adjacent ground.

runners_data.name: Perfect Location
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's three-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner and the race's pivot; won over 6f on Soft and placed on similar ground, so the conditions suit, and the uncontested lead is the key tactical weapon — the [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects a slight mismatch in the map rather than any fundamental concern about its chance from the front.

runners_data.name: Harry's Halo
runners_data.note: Six-year-old for Kevin & Lauren Frost returning after 84 days; two recent thirds on Soft ground over 6f and 5f show genuine aptitude for testing conditions, and this is arguably the most convincing soft-ground profile among the closers — the long layoff is the primary concern, as the trainer's 14-day record (0 from 8) offers no confidence of a sharpened-up returnee.

races.paceDynamic: Perfect Location is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press from the gates, is set to roll along at a sustainable clip on Good to Soft ground, controlling the tempo from the Epsom six-furlong start. That uncontested lead shapes this race as a wire-to-wire contest rather than a tactical battle, with the chasing pack — principally Em Four, Logi Bear, Harry's Halo, Twirler, Cayman Tai and Proof — all hunting the same piece of real estate from behind. The field holds more hold-up types than can legitimately close from the rear in one surge: Twirler, Cayman Tai, Proof and Harry's Halo are all true closers redistributed into midfield positions because there is simply nowhere else to put them, meaning the finishing straight will be congested with runners arriving together rather than staggered. This race shape strongly favours a front-runner or prominent racer who can control the fractions on a soft surface where natural pace is dampened, making Perfect Location's unthreatened lead the dominant tactical advantage throughout.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Perfect Location Controls Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Location secures an uncontested lead and dictates a manageable tempo on the soft ground.
scenarios.body: Perfect Location has won on soft and over six furlongs at a similar level, and with no rival capable of matching early speed, the fractions will be set to suit a horse who finds its rhythm alone in front; the soft ground only compounds the advantage by blunting the finishing kick of the hold-up pack arriving late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp the Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Location sets a genuinely strong gallop that over-exposes itself on the soft ground, opening the door for the hold-up brigade.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected pace would burn Perfect Location's stamina reserves on testing ground, allowing a clean-finishing type from the chasing group to reel it in through the final furlong; Em Four's one win and Logi Bear's recent second on similar going make them the most credible beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Runners Pick Their Way Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough to string the field out but the true hold-up types find clear daylight up the Epsom straight.
scenarios.body: Twirler and Proof, despite being mapped out of their natural rear position, both carry form on soft ground and at six furlongs, and a well-strung field could give them the gap they need; Harry's Halo's back-to-back thirds on soft going also makes it a credible player if soft-ground stamina becomes the deciding factor.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Slow Early Pace Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Location eases into a crawl and the entire field settles together, turning the race into a sprint off a slow tempo.
scenarios.body: A muddling early gallop on soft ground would compress the field, creating a sprint finish that suits horses with a sharp turn of foot rather than genuine closers; Cayman Tai and Proof are both lightly enough credentialed to spring a surprise if the race degenerates into a flat-out dash from two furlongs out.

watchPoints.text: Perfect Location — if it loads cleanly and jumps promptly, it could establish a lead so commanding on soft ground that no hold-up horse can realistically close it down in the final two furlongs.

Twirler, Cayman Tai and Proof — all three are true closers forced to race from a midfield position they would not naturally occupy; watch for crowding and interference in the straight as multiple hold-up types angle for the same gaps simultaneously.

Harry's Halo — the 84-day absence is the longest in the field and the trainer's recent form (0 from 8 over 14 days) gives little assurance it returns fully wound up, despite its strong soft-ground profile.

Logi Bear — drawn and ridden by David Probert who will be alert to any pace collapse; watch to see if Probert tracks Perfect Location from early on rather than settling deep, which would change its finishing position entirely.

Going — the official race going is listed as Good to Soft in the race card but the going report confirms Good to Soft across all Epsom races; monitor any overnight or morning update as any further softening would increase the advantage for front-running and soft-proven types.

races.name: Irish Ebf Restricted Maiden Stakes (for Horses In Bands C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Red Tail
runners_data.note: Showed ability when second over six furlongs on Good ground last time for Hannon, and now steps up to seven; the 13-length drift to 13th on debut at the same trip hints at inconsistency, but Leavy rides and the yard's form (0/37 in 14 days) means this is not a hot Hannon second-string moment.

runners_data.name: Artemis Star
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the field with a clear chance to dictate from flag to finish; Robert Havlin takes over for Muir & Grassick, who are in decent form (2/15 in 14 days), and the hood suggests she can be fresh — at 27 days off, she arrives fit and with the key tactical advantage of leading an uncontested pace.

runners_data.name: Lightenings Legacy
runners_data.note: Hold-up style with a very poor recent record (9th and 6th in last two) and headgear noted (visor), which suggests she has issues getting competitive; George Wood takes the ride but a true closer in a race likely to be run at a steady tempo is not an enviable position, and the form figures offer little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Taranis
runners_data.note: Unexposed debutant for Eve Johnson Houghton, whose yard is in decent touch (3/27 in 14 days); going unknown and style unknown — as an unknown quantity on debut, she could slot anywhere and must be treated as a wildcard; the market position on the day will be informative.

runners_data.name: Angel Of Desire
runners_data.note: Amanda Perrett's filly showed ability when fourth on her only start over seven furlongs on Good going — her natural style is genuine hold-up, but with more closers than the pace map accommodates, she is likely to find herself closer to midfield than ideal; Probert rides and the style-fit discount (0.90) tempers confidence in a race not truly run to suit.

runners_data.name: Golden Caturra
runners_data.note: Finished fourth and fifth in her two starts over six furlongs on Good ground for Gallagher, stepping up in trip here; Kaiya Fraser claims aboard, and as a genuine hold-up type, the steady pace likely set by Artemis Star makes this a difficult scenario — she needs more pace than this race is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Summer Triangle
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts over six and seven furlongs on Good ground are the form positives for the Moore yard (3/28 in 14 days), but she is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map because the field is rear-heavy; racing out of her natural position in a steady-gallop race, the style-fit discount applies and her chance hinges on a pace scenario that is unlikely to materialise.

races.paceDynamic: Artemis Star is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no natural rival to press her, she is poised to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good to Soft ground at Epsom over seven furlongs. The tempo is unlikely to be searching, which compresses the race and reduces the premium on raw stamina, favouring horses that can travel close to the pace and produce a sharp, contained finish rather than those who need a truly run race to make up ground from the rear. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate — Angel Of Desire and Summer Triangle are genuine closers who are likely to find themselves racing closer to midfield than their natural position, meaning their chance in a truly run staying shape is structurally compromised. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and those who can sit just off Artemis Star's shoulder, quickening through the final two furlongs without needing to make up significant ground — a steady-pace, positional, front-to-midfield profile is the one to side with.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Artemis Star Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Artemis Star leads without serious early pressure and sets a measured pace that rewards those racing prominently behind her.
scenarios.body: Artemis Star takes advantage of her position to dictate terms at a steady clip, leaving those held up with insufficient ground to make up in the closing stages on Epsom's relatively flat seven-furlong track; horses who settle close to her early can peel off her quarters and finish strongly without the acceleration demand of a truly run race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Rivals Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If one or both of the unknown-style runners (B Double U, Red Tail, Taranis) establishes a prominent early position and outstays Artemis Star through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A contested but still moderate gallop develops as Artemis Star faces a closer who tracks her through the bend, drawing the race into a battle of stamina and tactical gears; the horse with the superior finishing kick from a tracking position prevails as the front-runner ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely strong enough to string the field out and create space for a closer to make significant late ground.
scenarios.body: Angel Of Desire or Golden Caturra, operating closer to midfield than ideal, needs a searching tempo to generate the gap that allows a late run to matter — a scenario structurally weakened by the likely steady gallop and the redistribution of true closers into unnatural positions; this shape is possible but goes against the dominant race dynamic.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Moderate Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace causes the field to bunch and the race is decided by a blanket finish in the final furlong with no horse securing a clear advantage.
scenarios.body: With Artemis Star unwilling or unable to stretch the field and hold-up horses finding themselves too close to the pace to switch off properly, the race collapses into a tight, scrappy finish where positional luck and a clean run are decisive; a horse that finds daylight at the right moment benefits most.

watchPoints.text: Artemis Star to miss the break or get headed early — if she fails to lead, the entire race shape shifts and the probability weight must be reassigned to a prominent racer tracking closely behind.
Taranis on debut for Johnson Houghton — unknown style and going profile means she could emerge as a dark horse if she slots prominently; watch the market for late confidence signals.

Angel Of Desire and Summer Triangle may find themselves closer to the pace than usual given the hold-up congestion at the rear — if neither can switch off cleanly, they risk overextending early and weakening late.

The Good to Soft ground (confirmed for this race in the going report) is worth monitoring — several runners have Good-ground form only, and any significant change could alter stamina profiles through the final two furlongs.

B Double U's headgear and quick turnaround (13 days) for Dascombe suggests a horse being geared up tactically — watch to see if Jamin takes an aggressive early position that challenges Artemis Star's lead.

races.name: Betfred 'the Classic Bookmaker' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Morte Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist whose sole win came over this exact course-and-distance combination, giving him clear course claims, but his recent form shows poor consistency and his last six runs include a soft-ground ninth that tempers confidence; the 23-day break and blinkers noted in headgear suggest connections are trying to sharpen him up.

runners_data.name: Aurora Majesty
runners_data.note: Pierre-Louis Jamin takes the ride for Archie Watson (2 from 20 in the 14-day window), and this 4yo has placed twice in 12 similar-going starts; naturally prominent and well-placed to exploit a single-file pace shape, though soft-ground form has been mixed across multiple attempts at this trip.

runners_data.name: Kisskodi
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's 4yo boasts the best soft-ground strike rate in the field (2 wins from 15, placed twice) and has proven ability on cut ground at this trip; a genuine prominent racer, George Wood rides, and the horse's stamina on a softening surface makes it a key player if the pace is sustainable.

runners_data.name: New Vega
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and the race's only genuine pace-setter, giving him complete control of the tempo, but Simon & Ed Crisford's 3yo is 44 days since its last run and has managed only one similar-going start (unplaced); racing in its natural role but STYLE_FIT flag suggests the positional tags here need treating carefully.

runners_data.name: Rhoscolyn
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 8yo veteran has a flagged tendency to fade in the finish, and with just two days since its last run the turnaround is very sharp; a true hold-up horse whose best soft-ground figures (1 win from 15) do little to inspire confidence, and being remapped to midfield against its natural inclination further complicates matters.

runners_data.name: Naval Light
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's 3yo arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and has winning form on soft going, representing strong credentials for this shape; Sam James rides a horse who likes to come from off the pace — the race sets up well for a sustained late run if the tempo is honest enough to leave something to close into.

runners_data.name: Do Bronxs
runners_data.note: Loughnane's 3yo is a true hold-up type whose natural position at the rear is squeezed in this field — it finishes up mapped to midfield rather than where it wants to be, meaning it races out of its comfort zone; the STYLE_FIT discount applies, soft-going form is limited, and no wins from 10 similar-going runs underlines the concern.

runners_data.name: Velvet Rhythm
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's 3yo (4 from 38 in 14-day trainer window) is a genuine prominent racer who cannot secure that berth in a field already carrying Aurora Majesty, Kisskodi and New Vega ahead of it; Saffie Osborne rides a lightly-weighted runner whose two recent wins came on good ground, and the soft conditions add another question mark.

races.paceDynamic: New Vega is the sole confirmed front-runner and, on soft ground over Epsom's 7f, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop without any genuine pressure to destabilise the tempo. Aurora Majesty and Kisskodi will push to race prominently behind New Vega, giving the race a compact, single-file shape rather than a truly contested lead. The soft going will stretch the field out and reward horses who travel sweetly in the first half of the race rather than those who have to expend energy fighting for position. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses who can settle behind the pace and produce a sustained late run — Naval Light and Morte Point are the profiles this race is built for. The field also contains more prominent/hold-up types than the map can accommodate: Velvet Rhythm, Do Bronxs, and Rhoscolyn are genuine positional horses who will struggle to secure their natural berths and are most likely to be shuffled back against their will, with Aurora Majesty and Kisskodi best placed to actually claim the prominent slots.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Soft Solo Lead Sticks
scenarios.trigger: If New Vega dictates a measured, uncontested pace that never accelerates enough to string the field out fatally.
scenarios.body: New Vega sets fractions comfortable for him on the soft, the hold-up horses are denied the killer tempo they need and the race comes to them too late; horses close to the pace — Aurora Majesty and Kisskodi — are ideally positioned to pounce from second and third entering the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Devour Them
scenarios.trigger: If New Vega's lone-leader gallop is brisk enough on the soft to compromise those racing close to him, opening the door for a sweeping late charge.
scenarios.body: The prominent horses expend energy tracking a strong clip and tie up in the final furlong, allowing Naval Light and Morte Point to produce superior finishing kicks from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Fightback
scenarios.trigger: If the soft ground slows the pace to a crawl and horses on the pace conserve enough energy to repel any hold-up challenge.
scenarios.body: A falsely slow tempo means hold-up horses cannot make meaningful ground from the rear, leaving New Vega and the prominent horses to fight it out at a steady pace in front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Pace, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of Velvet Rhythm and Do Bronxs creates unexpected positional scrambling in the early stages that disrupts the expected race shape.
scenarios.body: The compressed field and soft ground cause interference and uneven splits, with a lightly-raced or freshened runner finding daylight at the right moment; Do Bronxs staying on from a position further back than ideal could capitalise if gaps appear.

watchPoints.text: New Vega holds the race in his hands — if David Probert lets him bowl along unchallenged at a soft-ground tempo, the horse could prove hard to reel in despite the STYLE_FIT flag.
Rhoscolyn's two-day turnaround is extreme for an 8yo — watch for signs of dullness in the paddock or early in the race, as a flat performance would not be a surprise.

Velvet Rhythm, Do Bronxs and Rhoscolyn may create positional interference in the early stages as they fail to secure their natural slots — watch for crowding behind New Vega in the first two furlongs.

Naval Light's back-to-back wins and soft-ground certificate make it the most interesting hold-up profile in the race — the key watch point is how well Sam James settles it and whether the tempo is honest enough to make ground from off the pace.

Kisskodi's soft-ground record (2W from 15, consistent placings) is the strongest of any prominent runner — if it gets a clean run through from second or third, George Wood will be riding with confidence entering the final two furlongs.

races.name: Betfred 'nifty 50' Amateurs' Derby Handicap Stakes (for Gentleman Amateur Jockeys) (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Sweet Reward
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old prominent racer who has won twice over 9-10f on Good ground recently, but today's soft conditions represent a concern given sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from 6 starts; Jonathan Portman's runner carries top weight and faces softer opposition, but the step up in trip and ground softness both work against him.

runners_data.name: Gordon Grey
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 12f on Good ground last season and has course-positive soft-ground experience (placed once from 2 sim-going runs); George Baker stable at 1/7 in a 14-day window is a positive angle, and Patrick Mullins is a capable amateur, but 86 days off the track is a query.

runners_data.name: Great Bedwyn
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with three places from his last five starts including a third over 12f on Good, handled by Richard Hannon whose yard is 0/37 in the 14-day window — the trainer angle is a concern; Good to Soft should suit on form profile, and Epsom's straight suits a horse arriving late.

runners_data.name: Son Of Man
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with genuine soft and standard-going stamina form, having won over 12f on Tapeta and placed twice on that surface from 15 sim-going starts; Jim Boyle runner who ran 19 days ago, and the drop to amateur company over a flat Epsom mile-and-a-half suits his late-running profile if the front-runners exhaust themselves.

runners_data.name: Epictetus
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with tongue tie and a tight turnaround (9 days since last run), managing only 1 win from 15 sim-going efforts; Jamie Osborne's yard is 2/11 in the 14-day window which is positive, but Epsom's unique track and the competitive amateur context make him hard to assess confidently.

runners_data.name: Divine Knight
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner from William Haggas, who is in fine 14-day form at 8/46; has placed three times from nine soft-ground starts and was third over 13f on soft in recent form, suggesting both the going and the trip are within range, though facing two rivals who will contest the early lead is a significant challenge.

runners_data.name: Devil In The Sky
runners_data.note: Prominent racer equipped with a tongue tie who has placed five times from 15 soft-going starts and has solid form around 12f in these conditions; the Gary & Josh Moore yard is active and 3/28 in the window, and Devil In The Sky's consistency (five 3rd-or-4th finishes) is both reassuring and limiting depending on whether this race sets up for a forward pitch.

runners_data.name: Yaa Min
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent runner with recent Tapeta experience, placing once from 12 sim-going starts; form over 12-16f suggests stamina is not an issue, but the move from standard surface to Good to Soft at Epsom is an unknown, and Hayley Burton's trainer record of 0/3 in the 14-day window offers no recent confidence.

runners_data.name: Damascus Steel I
runners_data.note: Front-running/prominent type who won twice over 12-14f on Good and has soft-ground experience at longer trips; Gihan Arnolda's small yard (0/5 in window) provides little trainer form, and Damascus Steel I will be competing directly for prominent positions with several other forward-going types, compressing his chance of getting a natural pitch.

runners_data.name: Dancing Tiger
runners_data.note: Hold-up/prominent type who has won twice on soft and placed four more times from 14 combined soft runs — the strongest soft-ground record in the field by win percentage; Roger Teal's yard is in decent 14-day form at 4/12, and Dancing Tiger's recent second over 12f on soft and win over 10f on soft confirm both stamina and conditions are aligned.

runners_data.name: Curran
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two wins over 12-14f on Good ground and fresh enough at 25 days since last run; Rod Millman's yard is 4/23 in the 14-day window, and Curran's proximity to a recent second and first over 12f means he arrives in form — but he faces direct competition for the lead from Gordon Grey and Divine Knight.

runners_data.name: Crooked Path
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has won twice and placed heavily on both soft and standard surfaces, with strong form over 16f suggesting stamina is his asset; the step down to 12f at Epsom may actually suit a horse who has won at 12f on Tapeta, and James Owen's 2/41 trainer window is low but the horse's own form is more compelling than the yard's.

runners_data.name: Edward Sexton
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up horse — his win came from a rear position over 14f on Good — who is mapped to midfield solely because the race holds more closers than the rear can represent; his style-fit score of 0.93 flags that he is unlikely to get his true position in this field, and the Gary & Josh Moore yard's recent 3/28 window is the more positive angle to hold onto here.

runners_data.name: Seeking Charles
runners_data.note: Has placed twice from 11 soft-going starts and his best recent form is over 12f on Good, but as a genuine hold-up operator placed into midfield representation by field congestion, the style-fit discount of 0.90 is honest; Mark Usher's 1/11 trainer window is unremarkable, and Seeking Charles is at his best when able to hunt down a real pace — which ironically this race may provide, if he can access the back-straight position he needs.

races.paceDynamic: Gordon Grey, Divine Knight, and Curran are all confirmed front-runners in a 14-runner field over 1m4f on Good to Soft ground at Epsom, virtually guaranteeing a strong, unrelenting gallop from the outset — none of these three will want to concede the rail or the early initiative. With three horses fighting for the same piece of real estate around Epsom's unique camber and turning layout, the pace is likely to be genuinely honest rather than falsely run, putting a premium on stamina and relaxed travel in the middle sector. The field also contains more prominent-racing types than the map can accommodate: Edward Sexton and Seeking Charles are genuine hold-up horses pushed into midfield representation simply because the rear is congested, and Sweet Reward, Devil In The Sky, Yaa Min, and Damascus Steel I will also be pressing forward, meaning those expecting to slot into handy positions will face a competitive early battle for them. On this race shape — a fast-run staying handicap where the front is contested and the ground is testing — the profile that benefits most clearly is the relaxed, well-positioned hold-up or late-midfield mover with proven stamina in soft conditions, able to pick off a tiring front rank in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Gordon Grey, Divine Knight, and Curran fight a genuine battle for supremacy and the soft ground compounds their early exertions, tiring in the straight.
scenarios.body: The three front-runners burn each other out through the first mile, leaving the track open for horses travelling smoothly in mid-to-rear pack to accelerate past a weakening lead; Epsom's unique undulations punish those who have used energy early and reward those who have conserved it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Pacesetter Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of Gordon Grey, Divine Knight, or Curran establishes a clear lead early while the others fail to sustain their challenge or get boxed in.
scenarios.body: A single front-runner who controls their own fractions on soft ground can dictate tempo to suit and potentially steal a winning break; Gordon Grey or Curran, both with recent winning form at this trip, are best placed to convert if granted a lone lead.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold Suits
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce enough to string out the field but not fierce enough to completely destroy the front rank, rewarding a horse racing just off the pace in a handy position.
scenarios.body: Sweet Reward, Devil In The Sky, and Damascus Steel I all press forward just behind the battle for the lead, positioning themselves to pounce as the three leaders weaken without having taken on the full energy cost of leading; soft ground form is key here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Caught Out
scenarios.trigger: If the pace settles into a moderate rhythm despite the multiple front-runners — perhaps after an early scramble that then steadies — leaving the true hold-up horses without a pace to aim at.
scenarios.body: Edward Sexton and Seeking Charles, already displaced from their natural rearward positions and carrying style-fit discounts, are the least likely to benefit and would need an unusually fast-finishing race to threaten; the redistribution of hold-up types into midfield means this scenario is further weakened by the absence of genuine late closers.

watchPoints.text: With Gordon Grey, Divine Knight, and Curran all wanting the lead, watch the first two furlongs closely — if they trade positions aggressively into Tattenham Corner, the winning time will be fast enough to compromise all three and hand the race to a mid-pack horse.

Dancing Tiger's soft-ground record (2 wins, 4 places from 14 starts) is materially superior to most rivals here and deserves close monitoring throughout the straight — if she travels smoothly behind the lead battle, Frederick Tett's hold on the position could prove decisive.

Edward Sexton and Seeking Charles are true hold-up horses mapped to midfield — if neither can access their natural rear-running position they lose their primary weapon, and backing either in a scenario that assumes a traditional late run should be treated with caution.

Damascus Steel I has front-running headgear (p) and faces a direct early contest with Gordon Grey and Curran — if he gets shuffled back early because he cannot win the battle for the lead, his form figures from further back are considerably less impressive.

Crooked Path's winning form at 12-17f on Good-to-Soft and Good suggests he handles varying conditions well, but his two wins came on Tapeta and his soft turf form (one third from 11 starts) is less convincing — watch whether the amateur jockey Mr Simon Walker can place him advantageously off a contested pace.

races.name: Stanley Wootton Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Hengest
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two wins over 10-12f on good ground; trainer Dylan Cunha has six winners from 26 in the last 14 days and Jason Watson adds class; soft-ground form is thin (1-from-9 similar-going), which is a mild concern, but tracking Trio from a handy position is ideal for his style.

runners_data.name: Almekarem
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse trained by Sir Mark Prescott, whose patient placing record is notable; recent win over 10f on good and strong form, but soft ground at Epsom historically causes traffic problems for deep closers and the large hold-up contingent increases the risk of a blocked run.

runners_data.name: Perfect Scoundrel
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid claims stepping back from 12f; recent wins over 9-10f on good and soft, showing stamina is not in question, and Amanda Perrett's yard has been lightly represented but in form; Robert Havlin steers a horse who will likely occupy the second or third position and may benefit directly from Trio's lead.

runners_data.name: Arthur's Realm
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran of eight years, consistent on soft ground (12 from 15 similar-going runs) with one win and two places; high weight and 87-day absence are concerns, but his soft-ground reliability distinguishes him from rivals; will need a clear run from the rear.

runners_data.name: Mao Shang Wong
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by inclination, though the weight of closers in this field pushes him into a midfield mapping position he would not naturally occupy; one win from 15 on similar going is modest, and Saffie Osborne will need an improbable amount of daylight if he is to deliver from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Double Red
runners_data.note: Prominent-to-handy racer with experience over 10-12f on good ground; Henry Candy's yard has been quiet (0 from 4 in 14 days) and the horse has not won on soft, but David Probert can position him just off Perfect Scoundrel to be involved if the pace relents late.

runners_data.name: Trio
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and race-shaper; three-year-old carrying 134lbs off just 17 days' rest, with recent back-to-back wins over 8f on good — stepping up to 1m2f on soft is the key unknown, and if stamina gives way late, she hands the race to prominent chasers behind her.

runners_data.name: Crystal Pier
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old holds a tongue-tie and is a genuine hold-up horse; previous win over 8f on soft (Sta) shows some cut-ground ability, and Hector Crouch is an able big-field reader; 42 days off and a step up from shorter trips require proving, but qualitative form is solid.

runners_data.name: Hello Cotai
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's five-year-old is a natural hold-up type whose best form comes off a strong pace; placed into midfield by the race's congestion at the rear rather than by design, so Pat Cosgrave faces the challenge of engineering cover without the natural rear-of-field berth Hello Cotai thrives in; soft-ground record (3-from-15) is uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Sail On Sailor
runners_data.note: Simon Dow's three-year-old has shown real ability — three wins in recent form — but is a hold-up horse by style, and the redistribution note is genuine; Joe Leavy inherits a rider-against-type problem, as Sail On Sailor must use his speed earlier than ideal, diluting the finish that has fuelled his winning streak.

races.paceDynamic: Trio is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no rival capable of sustaining genuine early pressure on her, she is set to control this race from the front at a tempo dictated entirely on her own terms over Epsom's 1m2f on good-to-soft ground. Hengest and Perfect Scoundrel will push forward to track her in a prominent position, but neither has the profile to unsettle her rhythm, meaning the pace is likely to be honest rather than searching — a controlled lead from Trio with a compact, manageable group behind. The hold-up contingent is large — Almekarem, Arthur's Realm, Mao Shang Wong, Crystal Pier, Hello Cotai and Sail On Sailor all want to come from off the pace — but with Mao Shang Wong, Hello Cotai and Sail On Sailor redistributed to midfield in the map because the field cannot physically accommodate all true hold-up horses at the rear, several of them will be racing out of their preferred position. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can track Trio at close range and pounce turning in, as a truly genuine pace is not guaranteed and the hold-up horses will have too much traffic and too little runway on Epsom's sharp finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Trio Controls, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Trio leads at a fair but not punishing tempo and prominent chasers track her to the turn.
scenarios.body: Trio sets a measured pace on good-to-soft ground, giving Hengest and Perfect Scoundrel a perfect tow into the straight; the hold-up horses lack the clear run to reel them in on Epsom's relatively short run-in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Trio Fades, Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Trio's lead becomes too strong and she ties up late, opening a gap for a quality hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: An honest early tempo from Trio drains her reserves on soft ground over a trip that stretches her stamina; a well-positioned hold-up horse who secures a clear passage off the home bend delivers the challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front-Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Trio bowls along unchallenged and the field fails to close, allowing her to steal the race outright.
scenarios.body: Absent genuine pursuit, Trio is never headed and the soft ground rewards her galloping style if she proves stamina over 1m2f; the hold-up horses are caught flat-footed with no pace to aim at.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Hold-Ups Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed midfield hold-up horses find daylight and the pace is strong enough to reel in the leaders.
scenarios.body: Mao Shang Wong, Sail On Sailor or Hello Cotai would need an uncharacteristically clear passage despite being shuffled out of their natural rear-of-field role; this is a low-probability outcome given their style-fit discounts and the compressed finish at Epsom.

watchPoints.text: Trio (Charles Bishop) — if she is allowed to bowl along uncontested in front on soft ground, she could prove very difficult to peg back and the race may be decided before the field reaches the short Epsom straight.

The redistribution cluster of Mao Shang Wong, Hello Cotai and Sail On Sailor — all three are true hold-up horses occupying unnatural midfield positions; watch for traffic problems and jostling approaching the final bend as they seek room that may not materialise.

Almekarem (Dylan Hogan, Sir Mark Prescott) — if the hold-up ground clogs early and he cannot settle towards the rear on his own terms, his ability to produce a late run will be severely compromised despite his apparent class.

Arthur's Realm — longest absentee in the field at 87 days and carrying a headgear (p) flag; monitor parade ring behaviour and early race movement, as a soft-ground specialist returning after a layoff can either strip fit or find the first furlong too sharp.

Perfect Scoundrel (Robert Havlin) — watch where he slots behind Trio at the start; if he secures second or third on the rail going into the first bend, his recent form over this trip on soft suggests he is the biggest tactical threat to the front-runner scenario.

races.name: Geoff Lewis Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Oj Lifestyle
runners_data.note: Tom Queally takes the ride on a six-year-old who has placed once from 15 starts on comparable going; though a natural closer, the hold-up traffic in this race means he will operate closer to midfield than his preferred position, which tempers how effective his usual race-reading will be.|

runners_data.name: Amused
runners_data.note: Four-year-old trained by Jim Boyle who ran just six days ago — quick turnaround for a horse whose last five starts show no wins and a string of placed efforts at shorter trips; genuinely a hold-up type by nature but will find the rear congested and must operate from a position slightly alien to his rhythm.|

runners_data.name: Here I Bow
runners_data.note: Three-year-old lightly campaigned at OR 75 by Oli Rix, returning 11 days after an eight-length defeat at a mile — stepping up in trip is a potential positive but the form at eight furlongs on Good or better has been modest and the team's trainer strike rate over 14 days is zero from five.|

runners_data.name: Super Hit
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a hood, trained by James Owen whose yard has gone 2/41 in the past fortnight — however, Super Hit has won twice over ten furlongs on Good ground and a prominent position against an uncontested front-runner suits his style well in this configuration.|

runners_data.name: Tronido
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, trained by Simon Dow, with two wins from 15 starts on similar going — he has soft-ground form at seven furlongs and Epsom experience, and an uncontested lead over a mile and a half on Good to Soft is the ideal scenario for a horse who thrives when able to dictate.|

runners_data.name: Eduardo Calderon
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent type from Harry Eustace's yard, which has sent out three winners from 16 runners in the past fortnight — the form is a string of placed efforts, soft-ground experience is proven, and Kaiya Fraser's claim of 3lb is a clear asset travelling just off a soft-paced leader.|

runners_data.name: Uniter
runners_data.note: Denis Coakley's three-year-old at the bottom of the weights on OR 58, with a pulled-up run in recent form and a soft-ground win in the profile — a true hold-up type by inclination, but the congested rear means Saffie Osborne will be forced to navigate from midfield, and the STYLE_FIT flag underlines the limited probability of this horse finding its best position today.|

races.paceDynamic: Tronido is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him from the off, he is expected to bowl along at a measured, controllable tempo over this mile and a half on Good to Soft ground at Epsom. Super Hit and Eduardo Calderon will push up prominently behind him, giving the race a reasonable but not brutal pace structure — the sort that rewards those who travel within themselves early and have something left on the descent into the home straight. The three hold-up horses — Oj Lifestyle, Amused, and Uniter — are true closers by nature but, with the rear of the field already crowded with that profile, they are unlikely to secure their natural position and will be shuffled into midfield instead, meaning genuine late swoops from the back are less plausible than the runner list alone might suggest. Key Lails and Here I Bow, both legitimate hold-up types, add to the bunching at the rear. With a sustainable pace set by an uncontested Tronido and the field compressed into a mid-to-rear cluster, this race shape most favours prominent racers who can control their position just off the leader and pounce as the track's undulations unfold — the Prominent profile is the one to be on side with.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tronido Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Tronido sets a steady, uncontested gallop and the race develops into a test of positioning rather than raw stamina.
scenarios.body: Tronido dictates from the front at a fair but manageable pace, with Super Hit and Eduardo Calderon travelling comfortably in his slipstream before the home straight offers them the opportunity to deliver their challenges; the Good to Soft ground at Epsom suits horses who travel prominently and hit their stride in the final quarter-mile rather than those making up ground from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tronido Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that Tronido's front-running gallop on Good to Soft becomes a stamina-sapping war of attrition that he controls throughout.
scenarios.body: Tronido, racing at OR 65 and already a course winner at 7f on Good ground, simply never gets headed as the field fails to coordinate a challenge through the straight; the soft-ish conditions and Epsom's unique undulating track drain the finishing speed of anything held up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than anticipated and Tronido gets pushed along, opening the door for the hold-up runners to close off the turn.
scenarios.body: Key Lails, the most straightforwardly placed hold-up runner in this field, would be the chief beneficiary if the early gallop quickens enough to leave something in the tank for a late surge; Here I Bow, lightly treated at OR 75, also carries claims in this shape if given a clear run down the middle of the track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield produces crowding and interference through Epsom's twisting straight, scrambling the race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With Oj Lifestyle, Amused, and Uniter all forced to race outside their natural hold-up roles and bunched together in midfield, any significant traffic through the home straight could produce a messy finish where an uncomplicated traveller finds daylight; Super Hit, wearing a hood and trained by a yard firing at 2/41 over the past fortnight, carries each-way interest as a composed sort in chaotic circumstances.

watchPoints.text: Tronido's uncontested lead is the single biggest tactical factor in this race — if Tyler Heard is allowed to dictate a comfortable tempo, he could be significantly harder to pass than his OR of 65 suggests.

The three redistributed hold-up horses (Oj Lifestyle, Amused, Uniter) will be competing for midfield space simultaneously — watch for crowding and cover problems through Epsom's uniquely winding straight, which could compromise all three.

Amused ran only six days ago and is stepping into softer ground than his recent starts — a quick turnaround with a fitness or recovery question mark in testing conditions is worth monitoring in-running for any signs of stopping abruptly.

Eduardo Calderon's yard (Harry Eustace, 3/16 in 14 days) is in form and the horse's placed efforts on soft and good-to-soft ground suggest the conditions are no bar — watch how quickly Kaiya Fraser positions him after the start, as getting the prominent slot early is critical to his chance.

Key Lails is partnered by Seamus Cronin claiming 5lb, and while the horse won last time, his record of zero wins from 15 starts on comparable going is a note of caution if the race develops into a genuine soft-ground stamina test rather than a tactical affair.

races.name: Betfred 'play Fred's £5 Million' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: French Affair
runners_data.note: Won twice at 6f on good ground and ran respectably at 7f, making the step up in trip a mild query, but Jennie Candlish's form with 3-year-olds and the naturally prominent style means this runner is ideally positioned to track Million Gold and pounce; good-to-soft going poses no concern based on sim-going record of 3/15.

runners_data.name: Dapper Guest
runners_data.note: A hold-up specialist who has shown little on similar going (1/15 in sim-going, 0 wins, 0 places) and a recent run just eight days ago raises fitness questions, but Saffie Osborne's claim could offset the weight; the horse's natural late style needs a stronger gallop than Million Gold is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Silver Trumpet
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's five-year-old has won over this exact trip on good ground and brings solid 7f experience, sitting naturally prominent which suits this steady-pace scenario — the trainer's 14-day strike rate of 3/27 is modest but Charles Bishop adds confidence; good-to-soft is within range based on sim-going.

runners_data.name: Million Gold
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's 3-year-old is the lone front-runner and last ran 65 days ago, which is a fitness flag worth monitoring, but the horse won at 6f on standard at Southwell and steps up markedly in class — the uncontested lead is its key asset and Robert Havlin will exploit it fully.

runners_data.name: Fresh Fade
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old that habitually races over 5-6f and has limited evidence at 7f (one run, finishing sixth), making the trip an obvious concern; Michael Attwater's yard is quiet (1/17 in 14 days) and Kieren Fox inherits a difficult brief from a hold-up position in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to cause a dramatic late collapse.

runners_data.name: Play Me
runners_data.note: Jim Boyle's four-year-old has won twice over 7f on good ground and the form string shows genuine ability, but this runner is a true hold-up type that has been pushed into a midfield position on the map due to field congestion at the rear — the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 signals it will likely race out of role, and the modest sim-going record (1/15) tempers enthusiasm on today's surface.

races.paceDynamic: Million Gold is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only six runners over 7f at Epsom on good-to-soft ground, Robert Havlin can dictate a controlled, unchallenged tempo from the gates — French Affair and Silver Trumpet will push forward into prominent positions but neither is built to pressurise the leader into genuinely punishing fractions. The result is a sustainable gallop that rewards those who travel well in behind rather than those needing a searching pace to bring their finishing kick into play. Play Me is a genuine hold-up horse that has been mapped to midfield because the field's back-end is already crowded by Dapper Guest and Fresh Fade, meaning its true late-running profile may be compromised by a lack of clear daylight. This shape — a lone, uncontested leader setting a steady pace over an undulating 7f — strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to the fractions without burning energy, and who possess the tactical speed to kick when the leader is collared in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Million Gold Controls Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Million Gold is allowed to bowl along unchallenged and sets a fair but not punishing tempo, the race unfolds as a sit-and-sprint from the two-furlong pole. French Affair and Silver Trumpet, both naturally prominent, are ideally positioned to track the leader and have first use of a pace that never gets truly fierce — prominent types who can travel comfortably and quicken off a steady gallop benefit most here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Collide Early
scenarios.trigger: If French Affair and Silver Trumpet both push hard for position early and apply unexpected pressure on Million Gold through the first half of the race. A stronger gallop than anticipated stretches the field and allows any runner with stamina reserves to grind out the finish — those sitting just off a suddenly honest pace gain an edge over those who burned too much fuel up front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Find Late Opening
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the home straight and the front runners empty simultaneously, creating a wall of beaten horses for late finishers to navigate around. Play Me, though mapped in midfield rather than its natural rear position, would need luck in running to pick off tiring rivals, and Dapper Guest would need to produce career-best form having shown limited sim-going evidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Fresh Fade Surprises Field
scenarios.trigger: If Fresh Fade, a 3-year-old running over a trip slightly beyond its habitual 5-6f range, benefits from a pace that flatters its hold-up style and the senior horses disappoint collectively. This is the lowest-probability outcome given Fresh Fade's limited form at 7f and modest evidence on similar going — it would take multiple fancied runners under-performing for this shape to materialise.

watchPoints.text: Million Gold's 65-day absence is the single biggest variable — if Havlin is unable to sustain the gallop in the final quarter-mile due to fitness, the entire front-running scenario unravels and French Affair or Silver Trumpet will sail past a flattening leader.

French Affair and Silver Trumpet are both drawn and inclined to race prominently — watch the first furlong to see whether they crowd each other for position behind Million Gold, as any early friction could compromise the rhythm of both runners.

Play Me's true hold-up style is squeezed by field dynamics — watch whether Donagh Murphy (7) elects to drop it out regardless of its map position, because if it settles at the rear it will need a much stronger pace than expected to reach the principals in time.

The going is officially Good to Soft at Epsom throughout the card — all seven runners carry an OK going flag, but Dapper Guest's single sim-going win from 15 attempts and Fresh Fade's 3-from-15 record suggest the surface may stretch their chances further than ratings imply.

Silver Trumpet won over this exact course and distance configuration (7f, good ground) in its most recent victory — monitor whether Charles Bishop angles the horse to the outside rail in the straight, as Epsom's camber rewards runners who find space rather than those caught in traffic.
